transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in to see me?

Hi. Thanks. I guess I came in because... well, I just keep feeling like I’ve really let my family down lately. I took on this mortgage, and it's just been weighing on me heavily. 

It's gotten to the point where every small mistake I make at work—I wait tables, so little things happen—it just feels like proof that I’m completely useless. It just makes me feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. So, yeah, I figured I should probably come talk to someone about it.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
It's been... well, it's been going on for about a year and eight months now. Basically ever since I took on the mortgage for the condo. That's when all this really started.
During this time, have there been at least two straight weeks where you also lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, along with changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy?

Yeah, definitely. It's been way more than two weeks of that. Most days there's just this... heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like I'm just going through the motions. I'm carrying plates and smiling at customers because I'm supposed to, but not because I actually feel anything good anymore. It's just heavy.
Over these past 20 months, has your mood stayed pretty much the same low level the whole time, or was there a specific period where things got noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

Well, it hasn't been exactly the same the whole time. I'd say the really low periods... the times where I feel so heavy and guilty about everything... that's been going on for about a year and two months out of the whole twenty months.

During the roughly six months when you weren't in that really low, heavy period, did you feel essentially back to your normal self, or were you still experiencing some low mood or other depressive symptoms most days, just less intensely?

Well, I wouldn't say I was back to normal. Even during those six months when it wasn't at its absolute worst... I was still dealing with it. For most of this whole time, even on the days that felt a little lighter, I've just been weighed down by that empty, guilty feeling more often than not. It's just always kind of there.
During that really low, heavy 14-month period, did you also notice trouble concentrating or making decisions, like at work or with everyday tasks?

Yeah, definitely. It's been really hard to focus. Like at work, I'm having trouble keeping the numbers straight on the POS system and the inventory sheets. I'll just stand there staring at the screen... knowing I've done this exact same thing for years, but I just can't trust what I just entered. It's like my brain just won't process it right.
During that really low 14-month period, did you notice any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I mean, I sleep about the same amount I always have. I don't have trouble falling asleep or anything like that. It's just the normal amount of sleep for me.

Before you took on the mortgage about 20 months ago, had you already been feeling low, guilty, or down more days than not for some time, or did this pattern of feeling down start right around when you got the condo?
No, I wasn't feeling like this before the condo. It really all started right around the time I took on the mortgage, about 20 months ago. Before that, I felt fine.
During this really low period, have you had any thoughts of death or of harming yourself?

I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes... like when I'm lying awake before an early shift, I just think it would be easier if I didn't wake up. Like, if I just didn't have to keep failing at everything, you know? It just feels like it would be easier.

Have you ever had a period of several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and felt like your thoughts were racing or you were unusually confident and impulsive?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. I don't get super energetic or feel like my thoughts are racing. And I definitely don't feel unusually confident. It's really just been this low, heavy feeling most of the time.
Going further back, before this whole 20-month period even started, had you ever had a similar stretch of low mood, guilt, or loss of interest at any earlier point in your life?

No, not really. I mean, everyone has bad days, but nothing like this. Before I bought the condo, I was generally doing okay. I never had a long stretch where I felt this down or guilty all the time. It really just started with the mortgage.
During that really low, heavy 14-month period, did you notice any changes in your appetite or your weight?

Yeah, my eating has been pretty all over the place. Um, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal at work. I just don't have an appetite. But then other nights, I'll get home from a shift and just eat whatever's in the kitchen... really just to feel settled. So it kind of goes back and forth.
Just to clarify the timeline—has this ongoing low, guilty feeling been present for a full two years or more, or did it really begin about 20 months ago when you took on the mortgage?
It really started about 20 months ago. That's when I bought the condo and took on the mortgage. Before that, I didn't feel this way. It hasn't been a full two years yet.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a single, first-lifetime depressive episode with onset clearly tied to a psychosocial stressor (taking on a mortgage) about 20 months ago, with no prior history of depressive or manic episodes. During the most severe 14-month stretch she endorses depressed/empty mood most of the day, anhedonia, excessive guilt/worthlessness, impaired concentration, appetite disturbance (fluctuating), and passive suicidal ideation without plan—six symptom domains meeting criteria for a major depressive episode of at least moderate-severe intensity. No manic/hypomanic episodes reported, ruling out bipolar disorder. No psychotic symptoms (hallucinations/delusions) reported, ruling out severe with psychotic features. Because this is her first and only episode (no prior discrete episodes), recurrent MDD is excluded, and because low-grade symptoms persisted even in 'better' periods without ever remitting to baseline, this represents one continuous single severe episode rather than dysthymia or intermittent recurrence.
